papers.abstractEn: We study the 305M-parameter audio encoder shared by Gemma 4 and EmbeddingGemma 2 (identical except for its final projection) for Saudi and Gulf Arabic speech recognition, without changing any of its weights. A frozen system trains only a 22.6M-parameter CTC reader over a mix of encoder layers; an adapted system adds 3.1M low-rank adapter parameters, a 41.5M-parameter hybrid CTC/attention reader and joint decoding with a sub-word language model. Against Cohere Transcribe Arabic (2.07B parameters), re-run on identical audio, the frozen system trails in word error rate (WER) but is statistically indistinguishable in character error rate (CER) on five of six human-labelled conditions, while running 3.4 times faster on CPU with greedy decoding. The adapted system is statistically indistinguishable in WER on a public Saudi customer-service call (19.20% against 19.27%) and on clean Emirati speech, is significantly better on telephone-coded Emirati speech, has a significantly lower CER on all six conditions of these sets, and beats a 0.6B recogniser fine-tuned on SADA in WER on all six; it still trails Cohere in WER on long-form Saudi speech. On a blind, human-corrected public call-centre sample it ranks 4 of 15 systems, behind three commercial APIs (significantly only one) and ahead of the other self-hostable systems by point estimate. An optimised joint decoder runs it at 139 times real time on one GPU. We also show that references made by correcting machine drafts favour the drafting system. Code and public-set results are released.

classification.tldr: 该论文在冻结的Gemma 4语音编码器上分别用CTC读取头和低秩适配器实现沙特及海湾阿拉伯语语音识别,以极小参数量接近商业系统性能并大幅提升推理速度。

papers.title: How Far Can the Gemma 4 Speech Encoder Go Without Changing Its Weights? Saudi and Gulf Arabic Speech Recognition with a Frozen and an Adapter-Augmented Encoder

papers.abstractEn: People look up a song by humming it, but also by whistling it or singing it with the wrong words. Published query-by-humming systems and benchmarks focus on hums and sung queries, and no public dataset pairs whistles or wrong-lyrics singing with song recordings. We study both query types with a melody-only retrieval system: a key-normalized pitch track embedded by a 5.2M-parameter contour encoder, with a spectral-peak tracker for whistles. First, a physics-grounded generator renders synthetic whistles and nonsense-syllable singing from the vocal melodies of 11,083 songs. Training on them raises top-1 retrieval of held-out synthetic queries against an 11,050-song gallery from 0.180 to 0.251 for whistles and from 0.193 to 0.264 for wrong-lyrics singing, but the gain does not transfer: on the MLEnd test performers the best synthetic-only model gets 210 of 339 real whistles right at top-1, against 214 for the baseline. Second, a closed-set fine-tune on real MLEnd whistles with performer-disjoint splits raises whistle-to-hum top-1 from 0.631 (95% CI 0.581-0.681) to 0.673 (0.622-0.723), on known songs only. Third, two further generations of synthetic queries also fail to transfer: melody-conditioned whistles and la-la singing from a commercial neural music model leave real-whistle top-1 at 0.631, and an open-source pipeline (YingMusic-Singer-Plus singing with partly wrong, mumbled or nonsense lyrics, a DDSP whistle synthesizer, and a melody-error model fitted on real performers) gives at best 0.619 (paired difference -0.012, 95% CI -0.038 to +0.015). Across physics-based, commercial neural and open-source neural synthetic data, nothing transferred to real whistles, which points to collecting real queries as the missing step. Code is public; models and data will be released.

classification.tldr: 该研究针对哼唱、吹哨和错词演唱检索歌曲的任务，系统评估物理与神经方法生成的合成查询数据，发现各类合成数据均无法迁移到真实吹哨查询，指出采集真实用户查询是关键缺口。

papers.title: Whistle and Wrong Lyrics: Synthetic Queries Are Not Enough for Real-World Query-by-Melody

papers.abstractEn: Audio-visual deepfake detectors are often trained under a single dataset or manipulation regime, but multi-source training collections may contain heterogeneous attacks and uneven source distributions. Training separate detectors for each source is inefficient, while a single shared detector may be biased toward dominant source-specific patterns. We study known-source imbalanced multi-source audio-visual deepfake detection using FakeAVCeleb and LAV-DF, where source identity is supplied during training and inference. To address this setting, we build on the Multi-Scale Cross-Modal Transformer Encoder (MSCT) and propose Pre-MSCT Shared-Private Feature Fusion. Our method routes \texttt{[CLS]}-augmented audio and visual tokens into a shared stream and source-specific private streams before the first MSCT block, while retaining its internal multi-scale self-attention (MSSA), differential cross-modal attention (DCA), and feed-forward operations. The shared stream models cross-source reusable evidence, while the private streams retain source-dependent residual variations. A domain-aware gated residual fusion module injects selected private evidence into the shared representation for the main fused prediction. Experiments under two controlled source-composition protocols show improved macro and worst-source AUC compared with the MRDF and MSCT baselines. These results support shared-private cross-modal discrepancy learning in the evaluated two-source setting with known source identity.

classification.tldr: 针对多源不均衡的音视频深伪检测，提出共享-私有跨模态特征融合方法，在共享流建模跨源证据的同时用私有流保留源特异变化，提升宏平均与最差源AUC。

papers.title: Shared-Private Cross-Modal Discrepancy Learning for Imbalanced Multi-Source Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection

papers.abstractEn: Few-shot audio classification requires audio--language models to distinguish variable acoustic events from limited labeled data. PALM's main formulation adapts encoded class representations without changing pretrained encoders, but its class representations remain input-independent and classification uses audio features without class-conditioned refinement. We introduce DF-PALM, a dynamic feature-space prompting framework that combines audio-conditioned class representations with asymmetric cross-attention for audio refinement. Class representations are conditioned after text encoding, held fixed across fusion layers for each input, and reused for final scoring. Both pretrained encoders remain frozen, avoiding audio-conditioned text-encoder passes. With PENGI as the frozen backbone, the main 16-shot evaluation covered 11 benchmarks and six baselines. DF-PALM achieved 80.69% mean accuracy and 80.32% macro-averaged F1, exceeding PALM by 4.11 and 4.30 percentage points, respectively. Paired benchmark-level tests supported both gains after Holm correction. Across four shot settings, DF-PALM achieved the highest mean accuracy and macro-averaged F1 among the four evaluated prompt-learning methods. The gains extended to LAION-CLAP and OpenFLAM, with significant improvements over PALM in both metrics. At 50 candidate classes, operator-counted inference floating-point operations increased by 0.39% relative to PALM. These results support instance-conditioned feature-space adaptation as an effective approach to few-shot audio classification. Our code is publicly available at GitHub https://github.com/sunyulin0421/DF-PALM.

classification.tldr: 提出音频条件化的动态特征空间提示框架，通过类表示注入与非对称交叉注意力改进少样本音频分类，在11个基准上显著超越PALM且计算开销几乎不变。

papers.title: DF-PALM: Dynamic Fusion Prompt Learning for Audio--Language Models

papers.abstractEn: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) detection from speech benefits from both paralinguistic and linguistic cues, yet model training is frequently constrained by limited data. Fine-tuning a large pretrained speech encoder can easily overfit, while a frozen probe leaves the encoder's task-relevant knowledge underutilized. Therefore, we propose Dual Task Vector Merging, a parameter-efficient method that adapts a frozen wav2vec 2.0 backbone using task knowledge learned outside the AD task. Specifically, we inject two task vectors, derived as weight deltas from emotion- and ASR-fine-tuned wav2vec 2.0 models, into each transformer layer. During AD training, only layer-wise merging coefficients and a linear classification head are optimized, updating less than 0.1% of the parameters required for full fine-tuning. Speaker-independent experiments on ADReSS and ADReSSo show that dual merging improves over frozen probes, LoRA, and full fine-tuning, in the main binary settings, and gives the best results when combined with LoRA. Evaluation on PROCESS further shows that our advantages transfer to three-class HC/MCI/dementia classification when paired with LoRA. Experiments under reduced training data (20%, 40%, and 80%) confirm reliable gains in low-resource settings.

classification.tldr: 提出双任务向量合并的参数高效微调方法，将情绪与ASR任务知识注入冻结语音编码器，仅训练不到0.1%参数即可提升低资源阿尔茨海默病语音检测性能。

papers.title: Dual Task Vector Merging: Leveraging Emotion and ASR Knowledge for Low-Resource Alzheimer's Disease Detection

papers.abstractEn: Speech recognition in real time in far-field conversational settings still incurs significant errors. Identifying potential error spans during streaming ASR permits a recourse mechanism where the speaker can be asked to repeat the affected content under cleaner acoustic conditions. We propose \sysname, a new framework for online error localization, that identifies spans likely to benefit from this intervention. Our supervision uses clean audio to estimate how the recognizer's output might change under improved acoustic conditions. We probabilistically align noisy and clean decodes using a pair-HMM to obtain soft supervision. These soft targets train a counterfactual gain scorer by combining a suite of acoustic and language features to produce token-level scores, that are further grouped into spans for targeted recourse. An LLM uses the ASR transcript of the repetition to revise only the selected span. At a precision of $70\%$, \sysname achieves the highest recall by identifying up to 52\% more erroneous tokens compared to the strongest baseline. Targeted repetition yields relative WER reductions of up to 24\% under a budget that accounts for both interruption frequency and the lengths of re-uttered spans.

classification.tldr: 提出面向流式远场语音识别的在线错误定位框架，利用干净音频软监督训练反事实增益打分器定位可疑错误片段，并通过定向重述将词错误率相对降低最高24%。

papers.title: Ask, Don't Guess: Targeted Clarification for Speech Recognition Errors

papers.abstractEn: Sanskrit verse recitation is governed by $\textit{Chandas}$, a strict prosodic framework defined by rhythmic $\textit{Laghu}$ (light) and $\textit{Guru}$ (heavy) syllables. Because existing Sanskrit speech datasets prioritize ASR or conversational TTS, they lack the metrical fidelity required for authentic verse synthesis. We introduce $\textbf{\textit{ShlokaDhara}}$, a 43-hour, multi-speaker Sanskrit speech corpus capturing diverse meters, recitation styles, and melodic variations. We specifically focus on $\textit{Text-to-Recite}$, a synthesis task explicitly requiring both prosodic accuracy and metrical correctness. Benchmarking state-of-the-art TTS architectures via an automated UTMOS (neural MOS) predictor demonstrates that XTTS-v2 achieves the highest perceptual quality. We further validate the XTTS-v2 generated samples using two paradigms: subjective assessments by 16 Sanskrit experts and novel empirical metrics, specifically, syllable-level $\textit{Laghu-Guru}$ duration analysis to objectively quantify structural metrical awareness. Ultimately, this work establishes a robust dataset and evaluation benchmark for prosody-aware computational Sanskrit recitation. Generated Samples: https://shlokadhara.vercel.app/

classification.tldr: 发布43小时多说话人梵语诗歌吟诵语料库，提出韵律与韵格双重评估基准，验证TTS模型在韵格感知合成上的表现。

papers.title: ShlokaDhara: A Multi-Speaker Sanskrit Speech Corpus for Learning Meter-Aware Prosody in Text-to-Recitation

papers.abstractEn: Automatic Speech recognition (ASR) struggles with Pathological speech due to persistent speaker-specific mismatch. In clinical and accessibility scenarios, only limited target-speaker data is typically available, making full model retraining impractical. We present a component-level analysis of LoRA adaptation in Whisper, investigating how adapter placement interacts with the model size, training efficiency and utterance-duration in single-speaker settings. Our experimental comparative study shows that while scaling reduces errors, it does not eliminate mismatch. Furthermore, the full attention LoRa provides the most reliable accuracy, and the best time--accuracy trade-off. Improvements vary across utterance length, with medium-length recordings benefiting the most, while short and long utterances remain challenging. These findings highlight the importance of adaptation placement and duration-dependent evaluation, under challenging, data-scarce personalization scenarios.

classification.tldr: 该论文在病理语音场景下系统分析Whisper中LoRA适配器的放置位置、模型规模与语句时长对单说话人个性化识别精度和效率的影响。

papers.title: ASR Personalization in Pathological Voice: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Duration Effects

papers.abstractEn: This paper presents the acoustic and aerodynamic extension of DYNARTmo, a dynamic articulatory model for visualizing and synthesizing speech production. Gestural control trajectories determine vocal-tract geometry, which is converted into an acoustic tube with nasal branching and effective lateral passages. A lumped aerodynamic network relates prescribed glottal motion and pulmonary pressure to airflow and supraglottal pressure storage. Phonatory excitation, oral friction, and glottal aspiration are synthesized as separate contributions. Frame-specific acoustic responses are combined by overlap-and-add, preserving response tails beyond individual control frames. Three German words, ``Tasse'', ``Muse'', and ``Lade'', illustrate the coordination of articulation, pressure, flow, and acoustic sources across vowels, nasals, laterals, fricatives, and plosives. The implementation has been optimized by the author primarily for sound recognizability; independent perceptual evaluation remains outstanding, and fricative-noise naturalness requires further refinement. The model provides an inspectable, articulatorily controlled production plant for future neural simulations of babbling, imitation, and early word acquisition. Further work will improve acoustic realism, reduce empirical source corrections, and extend the sensory information available to developmental learning models.

classification.tldr: 为动态发音模型DYNARTmo扩展声学与空气动力学建模，用重叠相加方法合成德语单词的语音，提供可用于神经发育模拟的发音可控语音生成装置。

papers.title: Vocal-Tract Acoustics, Aerodynamics, and Overlap-and-Add Synthesis in DYNARTmo

papers.abstractEn: Real-time voice cloning has enabled large-scale streaming deepfake and vishing attacks, while existing Network Detection and Response (NDR) solutions rely on GPU-based post-processing that requires buffered audio and generalizes poorly to unseen speech synthesis models. This paper presents SENTRY, a hardware-oriented, streaming trust engine for inline deepfake detection at the network edge. SENTRY employs an integer lifting-wavelet front end together with a bank of multiplier-free transforms, including wavelet-packet envelopes, Walsh-Hadamard sequency profiles, waveform micro-statistics, and long-term spectral features, designed so that acoustic analysis needs only integer add, shift, compare and bitwise operations. A supervised gradient-boosted tree classifier is combined with an unsupervised Mahalanobis out-of-distribution detector trained solely on authentic speech, and their outputs are fused by a lightweight logistic layer to produce graduated LOG, CHALLENGE, or DROP actions. Under a closed-set protocol, SENTRY reaches 98.75% accuracy at a 1.25% equal-error rate (EER) on WaveFake, with perfect separation of HiFi-GAN and WaveGlow; its supervised track alone achieves an AUC of 0.9994 (fused: 0.9993). On ASVspoof 2019 LA (attacks A01-A06) over an 8 kHz mu-law telephony channel, it reaches 94.75% accuracy at a 5.05% EER, with a supervised-track AUC of 0.9948 (fused: 0.9884) and per-attack EERs below 7%. In our prototype, the feature front end runs as bit-exact integer code on one Arm Cortex-A53 core, and the classifier and fusion stage are synthesized for a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC using no DSP slices, returning a decision 220 ns after a feature vector is ready. These results indicate that deepfake screening can be placed inline without GPUs or floating-point hardware; generalization to unseen generators is left to future work.

classification.tldr: 提出面向边缘设备的流式语音深度伪造检测引擎，采用无乘法整数小波特征与有监督加无监督融合分类，无需GPU即可实现低延迟高精度实时检测。

papers.title: SENTRY: A Streaming Edge Network Trust Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection

papers.abstractEn: Self-supervised speech models commonly consist of a set of convolutional neural network (CNN) layers used as a local feature extractor, followed by transformer layers. The CNN layers are computationally demanding, and are also similar across models and resemble the much simpler mel spectral features. We hypothesize that the CNN layers can be replaced by a simple, universal model. To test this hypothesis, we learn a two-layer feature extractor via distillation from one or more teacher models (HuBERT, data2vec, and WavLM). Experiments on SUPERB(-SG) benchmark tasks show that our model largely retains the performance of the teacher models and can also be used in an unseen model (wav2vec 2.0). Our feature extractor requires only 3% of the MACs of the CNNs, resulting in a $>$20% overall inference runtime reduction.

classification.tldr: 通过蒸馏将语音自监督模型中计算昂贵的CNN特征提取层替换为轻量通用两层模型，保留性能的同时降低推理运行时间20%以上。

papers.title: Toward a Universal Local Speech Feature Extractor Through Distillation

papers.abstractEn: We introduce Long Listening Thoughts (LLT), a framework for constructing post-training datasets that improves audio reasoning by pairing deliberate perceptual grounding with explicit cognitive behaviors. On audio understanding and reasoning benchmarks, large audio-language models (LALMs) are limited primarily by perceptual errors, yet existing post-training datasets rely on audio descriptions of limited diversity. Through a four-stage pipeline, LLT (1) builds multi-aspect dense audio descriptions spanning semantic, acoustic, and temporal information, (2) generates more challenging questions, (3) synthesizes incorrect reasoning traces, and (4) extends short reasoning traces into long ones via a thought-continuation strategy that elicits cognitive behaviors such as verification and backtracking. Using LLT, we synthesize 1.6M reasoning traces and train Qwen2.5-Omni-7B with a two-stage pipeline of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by direct preference optimization (DPO). This improves accuracy on MMAU Test-mini (71.5 to 78.2), MMAR (56.7 to 63.7), and MMSU (60.6 to 66.0).

classification.tldr: 构建LLT后训练数据合成框架，通过密集音频描述与长思维链生成1.6M推理轨迹，经SFT和DPO显著提升音频语言模型推理准确率。

papers.title: Long Listening Thoughts: Eliciting Open Auditory Reasoning with Deliberative Perception and Cognitive Refinement

papers.abstractEn: Voice agents built as cascaded automatic speech recognition (ASR)->large language model (LLM)-> text-to-speech (TTS) pipelines increasingly rely on conversational TTS: streaming, context conditioned models that adapt delivery to dialogue history. Such models are natural and expressive but offer little explicit control over how rare, trust-critical drug names are pronounced, because these entities are too infrequent, and their vocabulary too fast-growing, to be covered by any amount of pre-, mid-, or post-training. We retrofit phoneme controllability onto a pretrained conversational TTS model without any pre/mid-training, using an ARPAbet vocabulary exten-sion, continued phoneme-augmented supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and a training-free inference-time acoustic-biasing step. On a 7,500 clip clinical drug-pronunciation evaluation, our model raises strict Gemini-judged correctness from 54.6% (no phoneme augmentation) to 90.7%, outperforming every conversational and stateless TTS baseline on the automatic metric. Because no training stage sees a drug name, the entire evaluation is out-of-domain, so the gains reflect learned pronunciation rather than memorization. In a blinded, randomized human study, adult listeners judge 84% of our clips correct, versus 82% for the strongest baseline, with overlapping confidence intervals on a stratified subset. Across all 250 matched clips, Gemini agrees with the human majority on 84.8% of binary labels (k{appa}=0.57).

classification.tldr: 该论文在不重新预训练的前提下，通过音素词表扩展、SFT微调和推理时声学偏置，为对话式TTS模型增加对罕见药物名称发音的显式控制，将正确率从54.6%提升至90.7%。

papers.title: Pronouncing Hard Words: Phoneme Adaptation of a Pretrained Conversational Text to Speech Model

papers.abstractEn: Video-mediated conversational systems rely on synchronized speech and facial video, making audio--visual input integrity important for reliable perception. We study audio-frontend design in a fixed MRDF (Modality-Regularization-based DeepFake)-based pipeline with AV-HuBERT visual processing and an MSCT (multi-scale cross-modal transformer) fusion encoder. We compare spectrogram-style log-filterbank features with frozen wav2vec~2.0 and WavLM representations, dual-SSL fusion, executed depth, and shallow-layer aggregation. Across three training runs, full wav2vec~2.0 improves mean macro AUROC from $84.19\%$ to $87.19\%$ on generator-disjoint MMDF. Six-layer execution further improves detection, and learned non-uniform aggregation adds $2.53$ percentage points, reaching $90.61\%$. Shallow execution reduces measured inference latency relative to full-depth wav2vec~2.0 across the tested input durations; first-second evaluation reaches $86.85\%$ macro AUROC. In a single-run comparison, dual-SSL concatenation outperforms either single stream, while one-way cross-attention yields lower detection performance and higher latency than concatenation. Layer-weight analysis shows greater emphasis on early speech layers, while removing the selector's visual input has little effect on detection performance.

classification.tldr: 该论文研究音视频深伪检测中的音频前端设计，发现浅层语音SSL特征聚合在提升检测精度的同时显著降低推理延迟。

papers.title: From Spectrograms to Shallow Speech SSL: Audio-Frontend Design for Generator-Disjoint and Low-Latency Audio--Visual Deepfake Detection

papers.abstractEn: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) have extended their capabilities beyond lexical speech understanding to tasks requiring paralinguistic and non-linguistic audio understanding, such as emotion recognition. However, these models still struggle to reliably utilize acoustic information, particularly when it co-occurs with spoken linguistic content. Existing benchmarks do not clearly distinguish acoustic perception from higher-level reasoning, making it difficult to identify the source of these failures. To address this issue, we introduce VocalGrad, a benchmark designed to evaluate LALMs' ability to perceive low-level acoustic variations. VocalGrad formulates this problem as a simple binary classification of temporal change direction, enabling evaluation largely independent of higher-level reasoning or semantic understanding. Our benchmark results reveal a substantial gap in acoustic perception between human annotators and state-of-the-art LALMs: while human annotators achieve high accuracy, LALMs perform at near-chance levels. We further conduct linear probing to identify structural bottlenecks in these models. Our analysis reveals two distinct failure modes: for some categories, task-relevant information is preserved in internal representations but not utilized by the language model head; for others, the information becomes progressively less linearly decodable across model layers. Overall, our results reveal substantial limitations of LALMs in modeling acoustic variation under controlled settings and expose representation differences not observable from text outputs.

classification.tldr: 该研究提出评估音频语言模型低层声学感知的基准，发现最先进模型接近随机水平，并通过线性探针揭示其内部表征保持与利用失败两类瓶颈。

papers.title: VocalGrad: Evaluating Acoustic Perception in Audio Language Models

papers.abstractEn: Qwen3-TTS reports state-of-the-art zero-shot voice cloning, but its technical report leaves open how the model should be conditioned, how it behaves outside read speech, and how it fails. We characterise its two cloning interfaces, in-context learning (ICL) and X-Vector, against Chatterbox, XTTS-v2 and F5-TTS on read, meeting, emotional and air-traffic-control (ATC) speech, using eighteen objective measures, an LLM judge, a spoofing countermeasure and a listening test. Neither interface dominates: ICL clones timbre more closely from correctly transcribed references, X-Vector clones timing, and ICL degrades sharply when a short reference transcript is wrong. Domain explains four times more variance than system choice. Qwen3-TTS leads on intelligibility and pitch register but trails on prosody, and the objective measures rank systems differently from listeners. An off-the-shelf countermeasure flags its clones no more often than genuine recordings, and on ATC radio it fails for every system. Code and audio are released.

classification.tldr: 系统评测Qwen3-TTS在多领域语音上的两种克隆接口表现,发现条件方式与领域差异对性能和失败模式影响显著。

papers.title: Beyond the Benchmark: Conditioning, Domains and Failure Modes of Qwen3-TTS

papers.abstractEn: Speech and audio language models connect continuous acoustic representations to decoders pretrained primarily on text data. Most such models use MLP or Q-Former interfaces to map acoustic features into the decoder's input space, requiring the decoder to learn how to interpret the resulting representations. We investigate whether grounding these representations in the decoder's existing text embeddings can help it use acoustic information while better preserving its pretrained text capabilities. We present ConvexLLM, a general-purpose speech and audio language model whose C-Gate interface represents audio as continuous convex combinations of frozen text embeddings. ConvexLLM achieves an eleven-task VoiceBench aggregate of 75.36, the highest among the open-weight models we compare, and an MMAU Test-mini accuracy of 62.50%. Its largest margins over the baselines are on spoken knowledge and reasoning tasks, while the strongest baselines are more accurate on audio understanding and transcription. In a comparison with a 2B-parameter decoder, C-Gate achieves higher aggregate spoken-language performance than MLP and Q-Former interfaces, with text-task performance close to MLP and task-dependent tradeoffs in transcription and audio understanding. These results support convex combinations of text embeddings as a viable interface for general-purpose speech and audio language models.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出用冻结文本嵌入的连续凸组合作为音频到文本解码器的接口C-Gate，在保持文本能力的同时取得开源模型中领先的语音与音频理解成绩。

papers.title: ConvexLLM: Scaling Convex-Hull Speech Interfaces to General-Purpose Audio Intelligence

papers.abstractEn: Self-supervised speech models such as WavLM achieve strong spoofing detection performance, yet which layers encode the most spoof-relevant information and what acoustic properties they capture remain opaque. We present a layer-wise interpretability study of WavLM using the ASVspoof 5 database, combining three complementary analyses: (i) per-layer linear probing with attack-level evaluation across speech synthesis, voice conversion, and adversarial attacks; (ii) a canonical correlation analysis (CCA) linking layer representations to spoofing-relevant acoustic features; (iii) an exhaustive grid search over layer subsets showing that use of five layers outperforms full thirteen-layer pooling. CCA analysis reveals that, while most acoustic features peak in alignment with mid-layers and then decay, voice quality measures jitter, shimmer, and the harmonics-to-noise ratio show the opposite trend, with correlation increasing toward later layers. Embedding visualisations reveal that deeper layers capture a continuous acoustic similarity among attacks rather than discrete categories, suggesting these layers encode fundamental synthesis artifacts rather than attack-specific signatures.

classification.tldr: 该论文对WavLM进行逐层可解释性研究，结合线性探针、典型相关分析和层子集搜索，揭示中间层编码合成痕迹而深层表征攻击的声学相似性。

papers.title: Interpreting SSL Representations for Spoof Detection: a WavLM Study

papers.abstractEn: The recurrent neural network transducer (RNN-T) remains a practical choice for streaming speech recognition, but training requires large intermediate tensors. We present Flash RNN-T, a joint and loss implementation combining specialized kernels with optional tiled recomputation over the full alignment space and vocabulary. Tiled and untiled Flash form the entire measured throughput-memory frontier on medium and long workloads. On H100, untiled Flash achieves 24-39% higher throughput with 26-56% less memory than the fastest baseline on these workloads wherever it fits. Tiling reduces memory further through recomputation. On medium, tiled Flash uses ninefold less memory than that baseline at 16% lower throughput when both use one backward call per batch. On long, it fits where all tested alternatives with that backward schedule run out of memory with 80 GB. These comparisons use each implementation's lowest-memory configuration reaching at least 95% of its peak throughput.

classification.tldr: 论文提出面向RNN-T语音识别训练的高效联合网络与损失计算实现，结合专用核与分块重计算，在H100上显著提升吞吐并大幅降低显存占用。

papers.title: Flash RNN-T: Memory-Efficient Joint Network and Transducer Loss Computation

papers.abstractEn: Recent speech brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) increasingly rely on large models and complex multi-stage pipelines for neural decoding. However, in speech BCI, where training data are scarce, noisy, and expensive to collect, the benefits of model scaling remain unclear. This work revisits a fundamental question: are large models truly necessary for accurate neural decoding? We propose BEST (Brain-Encoding-Speech-Text), a two-stage framework for efficient neural-to-text decoding. Instead of relying on large generative models or phoneme-centric pipelines, BEST introduces hierarchical intermediate representations and a compact speech-oriented decoder that directly maps neural activity to text. This design preserves essential structure while significantly reducing computational cost, enabling robust generalization in low-resource settings and practical deployment under constrained resources. On the Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks, BEST achieves word error rates (WERs) of 6.19% and 1.62%, respectively, using only 3.85% of the parameters required by comparable methods. Beyond these results, we provide three key insights: (1) decoder scaling yields non-monotonic gains; (2) cross-modal alignment is more critical than model size; and (3) overfitting degards sequence-level performance. Representation analysis further reveals a consistent neural-audio-text alignment pathway.

classification.tldr: 提出一种两级高效神经信号到文本解码框架，用层级中间表示与紧凑解码器大幅减少参数量，在脑机接口基准上以3.85%参数量取得领先词错率。

papers.title: Do Speech BCIs Need Larger Models? Rethinking Neural Decoding beyond Scaling

papers.abstractEn: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) pipelines often normalize transcripts by removing filled pauses and punctuation and expanding colloquial forms, potentially discarding cues useful for dialogue act classification. We evaluate nine transcript conditions across six classifiers (TF-IDF logistic regression, RoBERTa, BERT, ALBERT, GPT-2, and BiLSTM) and three conversational corpora (Switchboard, ICSI MRDA, and SLUE-HVB), supplemented by multi-seed experiments, normalization controls, and real-ASR evaluations. Across five random seeds, heavy normalization reduces Macro-F1 in all 15 neural model-corpus combinations under the original preprocessing protocols. Removal using the original filler and backchannel lexicon consistently degrades performance on MRDA and SLUE-HVB but produces mixed effects on Switchboard. Punctuation-aware TF-IDF experiments show that punctuation removal reduces Macro-F1 by 0.036 on Switchboard and 0.078 on MRDA, demonstrating that the original linear baseline's apparent insensitivity resulted from tokenization. Restricting filler removal to um, uh, and erm preserves degradation on MRDA but largely eliminates the SLUE-HVB effect, where the original lexicon removes class-defining backchannel expressions. These findings demonstrate that normalization effects depend on preprocessing definitions, feature extraction, and conversational context, supporting task-dependent rather than indiscriminate transcript normalization.

classification.tldr: 系统评估九种ASR转写归一化条件对对话行为分类的影响，发现去除填充词和标点会丢弃语用信号而降低性能，主张应按任务定制归一化策略。

papers.title: ASR-Style Transcript Normalization Removes Useful Pragmatic Signal for Dialogue Act Classification

papers.abstractEn: Expressive speech synthesis can now change emotion within a single utterance, yet its impact on deepfake detection remains unclear. We introduce EmoShift, a benchmark comparing emotion-stable (AA) and emotion-changing (AB) speech to examine these effects while accounting for static emotion identity and acoustic confounds. It comprises 7,240 bona fide utterances from four source datasets and 9,720 synthetic utterances generated using four expressive TTS systems. Across seven detectors, we find that emotion changes can make synthetic speech appear more genuine, increasing spoof miss rates by up to 25.3 percentage points on OMG-Emotion at fixed thresholds. Conversely, emotion-changing bona fide speech increases false-alarm rates by up to 24.4 percentage points on IEMOCAP. Further analyses reveal detector-specific sensitivities to emotion trajectories, not fully explained by static emotion identity or splicing artifacts. These findings underscore the importance of emotion dynamics in deepfake detection.

classification.tldr: 构建语句内情感变化的语音深伪检测基准EmoShift，发现情感突变会使合成语音更难被识别、真实语音更易误报，凸显情感动态对深伪检测的重要性。

papers.title: Too Emotional to Be Fake? Intra-Utterance Emotion Shifts Expose Failure Modes in Speech Deepfake Detectors

papers.abstractEn: We show that forced aligners degrade on spontaneous, noisy real-world speech, and that fillers, laughter, and disfluencies corrupt word boundaries, impacting many downstream applications. We revisit the classical GMM-HMM aligner with upsampled WavLM features instead of MFCCs, explicit phone units for fillers and non-lexical vocal events trained on verbatim-annotated spontaneous speech, and a discriminative projection fitted on clean and noise-corrupted feature pairs to improve robustness. The pipeline is self-bootstrapped from 149h of curated audio without manual or external boundary targets. On conversational (Buckeye) and disfluent (FluencyBank) speech it reaches word-boundary MAEs of 20.6 and 76.9ms, 19% and 17% lower than the strongest of ten baselines. Catastrophic misalignments (>200ms) are 2.7 times rarer than Montreal Forced Aligners (MFA) best model even after widening MFA's search beam, which we show removes a large pruning artifact from its conversational error; event units halve the error next to laughter, while being meaningfully more robust than existing aligners.

classification.tldr: 针对自发噪声语音改进GMM-HMM强制对齐器，引入WavLM特征、填充词等非词汇事件单元和判别式投影，显著降低词边界对齐误差。

papers.title: Noise-Robust Forced Alignment for Spontaneous Speech

papers.abstractEn: As joint audio-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi-event composition, multi-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross-modal relations. However, current evaluations largely reuse metrics from earlier simple and unidirectional tasks. They typically evaluate an audio-video clip as a whole and rely on simple predefined relations, making them unsuitable for these increasingly complex scenes. We propose an event-centric evaluation framework that disentangles audio and visual events at the event level, analyzes each event independently, cross-validates relations across modalities, and aggregates the judgments into a coarse-to-fine, three-level consistency metric. The metric assesses global narrative harmony, event-level temporal synchronization, and fine-grained attribute alignment, providing a general formulation for audio-video consistency evaluation across diverse generation settings and cross-modal relations. We instantiate the metric as AVC-Reward, a trainable audio-video reward model. To evaluate the agreement between automatic judgments and human perception across generation paradigms and relation complexities, we construct AVC-Benchmark, which is primarily built from diverse positive and negative samples generated by various types of audio-video generation models. AVC-Reward achieves state-of-the-art alignment with human judgment among automatic methods, provides interpretable rationales that localize failures, and improves the audio-video consistency of a joint generation model when used as an online reinforcement-learning signal. Project page: https://tsuki0512.github.io/AVC-Reward.github.io/

classification.tldr: 提出以事件为中心的音视频一致性评测框架与可训练奖励模型 AVC-Reward，其与人类判断最一致并能提升联合生成模型的音视频一致性。

papers.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation

papers.abstractEn: Neural watermarking systems are typically trained as tightly coupled embedder-detector pairs and implicitly assume static deployment. In real-world deployments, embedders and detectors are frequently updated and selectively decoupled for security and versioning purposes, which can break detection in previously embedded content and, more critically, increase false-positive rates on embedders that a given detector is intentionally not intended to recognize. In this paper the concept of backward compatibility in zero-bit audio watermarking is formalized. A training framework is proposed that pairs a new detector with a sequence of frozen legacy embedders (its legacy chain), using a performance-weighted sampling strategy so that the detector retains accuracy across all earlier versions. This coupling, while necessary for backward compatibility, is shown to induce an embedder-collapse effect that catastrophically degrades the true negative rate (TNR) against out-of-chain embedders. To counteract this, a Angular Diversity Loss (ADL) is introduced that explicitly forces each new embedder to occupy a distinct region of the output space. The combined approach restores near-perfect TNR with no measurable cost to detection accuracy or perceptual audio quality.

classification.tldr: 本文形式化零比特神经音频水印的后向兼容问题，提出遗留链训练框架与角度多样性损失，在不损失检测精度下恢复极高真负率。

papers.title: Backward Compatibility in Zero-Bit Neural Audio Watermarking

papers.abstractEn: Recent post-training approaches have shown that self-supervised speech encoders can be adapted to learn a single utterance-level speech attribute through knowledge distillation. In this work, we investigate whether a single speech encoder can simultaneously preserve multiple complementary utterance-level speech representations. We propose a multi-attribute multi-teacher distillation framework that learns semantic, speaker, language, and emotion representations from four frozen teacher models using a shared SSL backbone and attribute-specific branches. Experiments on multilingual semantic retrieval, speaker verification, language identification, and speech emotion recognition show that the proposed model achieves performance close to dedicated single-task students while requiring only a single shared encoder. Furthermore, the learned layer aggregation strategies reveal that different speech attributes naturally emerge at different depths of the SSL encoder, providing new insights into the organization of speech representations.

classification.tldr: 该论文提出多属性多教师蒸馏框架，用一个共享 SSL 语音编码器同时学习语义、说话人、语言和情感四种表示，性能接近单任务学生模型，并揭示不同语音属性在编码器不同深度自然涌现。

papers.title: Learning Speech Attribute Representations via Multi-Teacher Distillation

papers.abstractEn: Sparse routing reduces per-token computation but leaves the full expert bank resident in memory. We study expert pruning for speech-centric omni-modal models, where pooling calibration statistics can obscure the different expert demands of acoustic-input processing and text-answer generation. We propose PW-Pruning, a phase-aware extension of DO-ACP that constructs separate importance-weighted kernels for acoustic-prefill and teacher-forced answer tokens, then combines phase-weighted log-determinant marginal gains to select one static expert bank. On Qwen3-Omni, retaining 32 of 128 experts per layer improves MMAU-mini and MMSU accuracy over matched pooled selection by 3.20 and 4.38 percentage points, respectively, after supervised fine-tuning, averaged over three runs. Single-phase and shuffled-label controls on this public backbone suggest that semantic phase information contributes to these gains. Experiments on a non-public Qwen3.5-Omni backbone and English-only zero-shot evaluation of Nemotron provide complementary evidence. Across the tested Qwen budgets, AU gains are larger under stronger pruning, without inference-time mask switching.

classification.tldr: 该工作提出区分声学预填充与文本生成两个阶段的专家剪枝方法，在Qwen3-Omni上仅保留每层128个专家中的32个仍能提升多模态理解准确率。

papers.title: PW-Pruning: Phase-Aware Expert Selection for Speech-Centric Omni-Modal Models

papers.abstractEn: Audio-visual speech enhancement (AVSE) leverages visual cues to recover target speech from mixtures corrupted by reverberation, noise, and overlapping speakers. We propose a coarse-to-fine two-stage AVSE framework. In the first stage, a progressive SPAV-TFGridNet is extended to two synchronized visual streams to produce visually ordered coarse estimates by progressively suppressing interfering speech while preserving target reverberation and shared background noise. In the second stage, a TFGridNet-based target speaker refinement network takes the original mixture and both coarse estimates as input to further recover target speech and improve signal quality. The coarse and refined estimates are finally combined using development-set-calibrated fusion. On the ISCSLP 2026 Real-World AVSE Challenge, our system tied for first place on Track 1 and ranked second on Track 2 in OVRL, while achieving the lowest CER on both tracks at 12.31% and 14.79%, respectively.

classification.tldr: 提出粗到细两阶段视听语音增强框架，结合目标说话人细化与校准融合，在真实场景AVSE挑战赛两赛道分别获并列第一和第二。

papers.title: CF-AVSS: A Coarse-to-Fine Audio-Visual Speech Separation Framework with Target-Speaker Refinement and Post-Fusion for Real-World AVSE Challenge

papers.abstractEn: Audio-enabled large language models (AuLLMs) allow users to interact with them simply by talking to them, without the need for an intermediate transcription. This expands the model's accessibility and capabilities by encoding non-verbal cues. However, using non-verbal cues may lead to biased behaviour based on the attributes inferred (or assumed) from them. In this work, we focus on the gender attribute and show that models' perception of it can be unlearned using adversarial methods without a loss in performance on other benchmarked tasks. Such models are useful in situations where gender inference is unwanted. However, in other practical settings, gender perception (without bias) may be desired.As a less radical measure, we distil the gender-agnostic model, creating a model that perceives gender but responds similarly to the gender-agnostic teacher, unless explicitly asked.We apply our newly proposed methods to three AuLLMs and obtain satisfactory results in the gender-unlearning part and partially satisfactory results in the distilling part.

classification.tldr: 研究语音大模型从副语言线索推断性别带来的偏见，提出对抗性去性别学习方法及蒸馏出可感知性别但响应一致温和的模型，在三个模型上验证了方法有效性。

papers.title: Bias Mitigation in Audio-Enabled LLMs through Adversarial Training and Distillation Methods

papers.abstractEn: Large audio language models (LALMs) have made substantial progress in audio understanding. However, in high-throughput applications requiring frequent selection, judgment, and scoring, autoregressive text generation introduces additional computational overhead and response latency. To address this limitation, we introduce Qwen-Audio-Jev by augmenting Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR-Flash-Next with a dedicated Jev decision head. The model unifies selection, binary judgment, and scoring through three decision primitives: CHOICE, NOUL, and SCORE. Given audio, a natural-language question, and an explicit answer specification, it directly produces a task-conditioned probability distribution or a numerical score through typed decision readouts. Evaluation across 18 labeled configurations covers all three primitives: for CHOICE, Qwen-Audio-Jev achieves accuracies of 78.70% on MMAU-mini and 84.06% on MMSU; for NOUL, it achieves an equal error rate of 6.50% on the VoxCeleb1-O speaker verification benchmark; and for SCORE, the model achieves a normalized mean absolute error of 0.1062 on NISQA overall quality assessment, with Pearson and Spearman correlations of 0.8210 and 0.8074, respectively. Compared with the original Qwen-Audio-3.1-ASR-Flash-Next, Qwen-Audio-Jev achieves an approximately 20x inference speedup. It demonstrates its potential for efficient, high-throughput audio decision-making in applications such as large-scale audio screening, speaker verification, and automated quality assessment.

classification.tldr: 在音频大模型上加入类型化决策头，统一选择、判断与打分三种音频任务，实现约20倍推理加速并保持有竞争力的精度。

papers.title: Qwen-Audio-Jev: A Unified Interface for Audio Decisions

papers.abstractEn: Joint Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC) and Audio Tagging (AT) models traditionally rely on unconstrained multihead architectures. However, this design ignores the natural hierarchical dependency between sounds and acoustic scenes. In this work, we investigate a hierarchical (sequential) conditioning paradigm that predicts scene categories directly from intermediate event probabilities. Through a large-scale empirical benchmark with 66 full training runs across three state-of-the-art backbones (PaSST, PANNs, and BEATs) and different loss-weighting settings (beta in [0.0, 1.0]), we show that hierarchical conditioning achieves competitive classification performance while altering multitask optimization dynamics. Unlike multihead baselines, which sequentially solve the easier ASC task before optimizing AT, the hierarchical architecture enables synchronized dual-task learning for specific loss-weighting settings (beta in [0.6, 0.9]). Furthermore, we propose a multi-perspective interpretability framework that combines an analysis of the information bottleneck, manifold geometry, and Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) on a Term-Frequency Inverse-Document-Frequency (TF-IDF) event representation, providing complementary insights into event-scene relationships. Our findings reveal that hierarchical conditioning systematically yields lower conditional entropy, higher mutual information, and superior latent cluster separability (higher Silhouette scores), establishing a more structured and semantically faithful intermediate feature space.

classification.tldr: 该论文研究声学场景分类与音频标注的层级条件化多任务范式，通过大规模基准与信息瓶颈、流形几何等多视角可解释性分析，证明其形成更有结构且语义更忠实的中间特征空间。

papers.title: Hierarchical Interpretable Multitask Audio Representation Learning: An Analysis of Event-Scene Relationships through the Information Bottleneck

papers.abstractEn: Transcribing expressive piano performances into scores requires interpreting individual note timings within an underlying metrical structure. However, score attributes are associated with notes, whereas beats may occur without coincident note onsets. We introduce DuET, a Dual-Encoder Transformer that jointly learns note-level performance MIDI-to-score (PM2S) transcription and frame-level beat and downbeat tracking. Bidirectional cross-attention connects note and frame encoders, while an autoregressive decoder alternates between their representations to predict structured score attributes. We further introduce TimeRoPE and Time-Pitch Rotary Positional Encoding (TPRoPE) to establish a shared performance-time reference and explicitly encode relative temporal and pitch relationships. Evaluations on ASAP, a classical piano dataset, and our curated Gangqinpu dataset, which spans multiple genres with a focus on popular piano music, demonstrate improvements in score timing and notated duration. Compared with the strongest baseline on each dataset, DuET reduces MUSTER mean error from 6.56% to 3.64% on Gangqinpu and from 11.30% to 11.22% on ASAP. Ablations support the benefits of frame-level context, time-based positional encoding, and decoder-history masking. Code, weights, and demos are available at https://github.com/wei-zeng98/DuET.

classification.tldr: 提出双编码器Transformer联合学习音符级钢琴演奏转谱与帧级节拍跟踪，并引入时间与音高的旋转位置编码，在多个钢琴数据集上显著降低乐谱时间误差。

papers.title: DuET: Note-Frame Dual Encoding for Piano Performance-to-Score Transcription

papers.abstractEn: Human face-to-face conversation requires coordinating speech, gestures and expressions across both speaking and listening. We present ELLSA 2, an end-to-end full-duplex dialogue model that jointly optimizes speech interaction and streaming gesture-expression generation. An autoregressive, chunk-wise synthesizer combines pretrained acoustic features with distinct listening and speaking hidden states from the dialogue backbone and speech synthesizer, enabling continuous non-verbal generation even when the model is verbally silent. To translate dialogue understanding into vivid semantic gestures, we introduce contextual semantic calls and template guidance, separating whether to invoke an available semantic gesture from how to realize it. We also establish a curated data and evaluation pipeline for dialog-aware co-speech gesture generation and investigate reference-based multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as automatic judges. Experiments show that ELLSA 2 remains highly competitive with open-source full-duplex speech interaction models and outperforms cascaded baselines across dialog-aware gesture and expression metrics. Semantic template guidance further significantly improves semantic gesture quality. Strong system-level correlations with human judgments support these reference-based scores as useful preliminary metrics for full-duplex and semantic gesture assessment. Together, these results advance dialogue modeling from spoken responses toward coordinated multimodal interaction.

classification.tldr: 提出端到端全双工对话模型，联合优化语音交互与流式手势表情生成，通过语义调用与模板指导提升语义手势质量，并建立基于参考的多模态自动评测方法。

papers.title: Full-Duplex Interaction with Speech, Expressions and Gestures

papers.abstractEn: In automatic speech recognition (ASR), transcription errors with similar lexical or semantic discrepancies can have markedly different consequences for the situation conveyed by speech. Capturing these differences requires not merely contextual assessment, but an understanding of what the spoken discourse describes, establishes, or seeks to bring about. However, relying on LLM judges introduces computational cost and scoring variability. We introduce SITAR, a situational distortion metric for ASR, realized through a comprehensive end-to-end construction framework. Specifically, this framework aggregates situational severity and cumulative extent into a unified score via a bounded recursive formulation. Using targets derived from this formulation with limited offline LLM support, we train SITAR as a lightweight BERT-family regressor that scores reference-hypothesis pairs in a single forward pass, entirely free of any prohibitive runtime costs. Recognizing that introducing a new metric demands rigorous justification, we formalize a principled validation protocol spanning both extrinsic validity, assessed at macro and micro levels, and intrinsic scorer reliability. The former, evaluated across diverse datasets and models, demonstrates that SITAR reliably tracks broad capability scaling while providing orthogonal diagnostic utility, whereas the latter, examined on a purpose-built controlled benchmark, confirms the operational soundness of the scoring instrument itself. Through systematic validation, we demonstrate that SITAR holds strong potential as a practical, lightweight complement to existing ASR metrics. We will release the full recipes (code, model weights, dataset, etc.) after the internal review to support community research.

classification.tldr: 提出一种面向语音情境失真的轻量级ASR评测指标，通过有界递归公式聚合严重度与累积程度，并建立涵盖外在效度与内在可靠性的系统验证协议。

papers.title: SITAR: A Situational Distortion Metric for Automatic Speech Recognition Evaluation

papers.abstractEn: Detecting depression from speech in elderly patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is complicated by overlapping acoustic effects of cognitive decline. Without disentangling these, classifiers risk learning cognitive rather than depression-specific patterns. We present a Korean elderly speech corpus of 89 MCI speakers collected over three years with concurrent depression (SGDS) and cognitive (MMSE) assessments. Both linear mixed-effects models and partial correlations identify the same pattern: of seven feature groups, only formant features are associated with depression after controlling for cognitive function, while widely used F0 features carry no signal. The F1+F2 subset achieves UAR 0.760 with just 12 features, outperforming both the full eGeMAPS baseline and self-supervised representations. These findings show that concurrent clinical assessments can identify interpretable, depression-specific acoustic markers in populations where cognitive and affective symptoms co-occur.

classification.tldr: 该研究构建了带同步临床评估的韩国老年语音语料库，通过控制认知功能分离出抑郁特异声学标记，发现仅共振峰特征有效且12个特征即可达0.760 UAR。

papers.title: Disentangling Depression from Cognitive Decline in Elderly Speech Using Concurrent Clinical Assessments

papers.abstractEn: Dementia severely impairs communication abilities and turns everyday conversations into challenging experiences. Individuals affected by dementia frequently struggle to express their thoughts or complete sentences, making it difficult for family members and caregivers to understand their needs. This study proposes a novel approach to assist dementia patients by developing an integrated system that detects signs of dementia through Bangla speech and text analysis and provides sentence auto-completion support during conversations. To achieve this, recorded voices from individuals with and without dementia were analysed, and key acoustic features were extracted to capture vocal patterns associated with cognitive decline. A transformer-based model was employed to transcribe voice signals into text for linguistic analysis. In the classification task, several Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models were evaluated using both acoustic and textual representations, and the LSTM model architectures demonstrated strong capabilities for modelling contextual patterns in speech and language data. For the sentence auto-completion task, a sequential learning model based on a Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM) network with an attention mechanism was developed to sequentially complete partially expressed Bangla sentences during conversation. This research bridges the gap in dementia analysis in an underrepresented language and implements a sentence auto-completion framework for cognitive disorders.

classification.tldr: 针对孟加拉语失智症辅助场景，构建基于Transformer的语音识别与Bi-LSTM注意力句子自动补全系统，实现语音检测与对话补句支持。

papers.title: Automatic Sentence Completion Using Bengali Audio Speech with a Transformer-Based Early Speech Recognition System

papers.abstractEn: Spoken Dialogue Models (SDMs) typically share a speech-token space for generation and synthesis, leading to long autoregressive sequences and costly inference. Lower-rate speech tokenizers shorten sequences but may introduce compression-quality trade-offs and costly replacement without breaking this coupling. To address this limitation, we propose CoSTA, a compatibility-preserving post-hoc framework that decouples generation and synthesis token spaces while retaining the original speech tokenizer and decoder. CoSTA extends the generation token space with compressed representations via mean-initialized vocabulary extension, pronunciation adaptation, and dialogue adaptation, followed by deterministic expansion back to the original speech-token space before synthesis. On bilingual speech-dialogue benchmarks, CoSTA achieves approximately $1.7\times$ expanded speech-token generation speed, lower full-response latency, and higher throughput while preserving response quality. Analyses show more sustained interaction under limited budgets and a practical trade-off among compression, decoding efficiency, and quality. Further experiments demonstrate cross-architecture transfer and complementarity to low-rate tokenization.

classification.tldr: 提出CoSTA后处理框架，将口语对话模型的生成与合成语音token空间解耦，用压缩token加速生成，实现约1.7倍生成提速并保持响应质量。

papers.title: CoSTA: Compressed Speech Token Adaptation for Efficient Spoken Dialogue Models

papers.abstractEn: Speaking-style captioning (SSC) aims to generate natural language descriptions of how speech is delivered, capturing paralinguistic attributes such as vocal timbre, prosody, and expressivity. Many downstream applications, including conversational AI agents, controllable speech generation, and large-scale audio annotation, require dimension-specific style captions that describe targeted aspects of speech (e.g., speaker traits, emotion, or delivery style), rather than a single undifferentiated description. However, existing work lacks a unified formulation for controllable speaking-style captioning. We address this gap by formulating SSC as an instruction-following audio-language task, where explicit instructions specify the speaking-style dimensions to be described. We introduce StyleInstructCaps, the first standardized benchmark for controllable speaking-style captioning in audio-language models. StyleInstructCaps provides a dataset and evaluation framework that measures metadata groundedness, hallucination, instruction-following ability, generalization to unseen instructions and audio datasets, and speaker-style consistency. Across nine state-of-the-art audio-language models, we find that strong instruction-following ability does not necessarily imply grounded speaking-style understanding, and that SSC-specific instruction-diverse training substantially improves groundedness, controllability, and speaker consistency.

classification.tldr: 提出了首个可控说话风格描述的标准化基准StyleInstructCaps，评测显示指令跟随能力并不等同于有依据的风格理解，而风格指令训练能显著提升可控性。

papers.title: A Benchmark for Controllable Speaking-Style Captioning in Audio-Language Models

papers.abstractEn: Identifying individual dogs from barks in real-world videos remains challenging and largely unexplored. Solving this problem would enable long-term behavioral analysis, veterinary monitoring, and animal welfare monitoring by attributing vocalizations and behaviors to the correct individual. Real-world videos are challenging because multiple dogs may bark simultaneously, become occluded, or move in and out of view. Prior studies show that canine vocalizations and visual appearance contain discriminative identity information, but these modalities have largely been studied independently. We present a multimodal dog-fingerprinting framework combining visual identification, multiple-object tracking, and canine vocal fingerprinting to associate bark events with individual dogs while maintaining persistent profiles. The framework synchronizes bark events with tracked dogs and updates profiles using visual appearance and vocal characteristics, enabling identification despite occlusion, overlapping vocalizations, and off-screen barking. We also introduce a benchmark of 46 real-world videos containing 213 manually annotated bark events. Our framework correctly localizes the active visible dog in 61.83% of visible events at IoU $\geq 0.30$ and achieves a 91.33% F1 score for visible versus off-screen barking detection.

classification.tldr: 该文提出结合视觉识别、多目标跟踪与犬类声音指纹的多模态框架，在真实视频中把吠叫事件关联到具体个体犬只，并发布了含213条标注吠叫事件的基准。

papers.title: Audio-Visual Dog Identification and Tracking in Real-World Videos

papers.abstractEn: Unsupervised speech denoising methods such as MixIT and noisy-target training can be trained directly on noisy recordings, avoiding the sim-to-real gap of synthetic training data, but remain well below supervised performance. Teacher--student self-training, as in RemixIT, narrows this gap by remixing a teacher's estimates into new mixtures that supervise a student; however, since the student is trained only toward the teacher's estimates, teacher errors, in particular over-suppressed speech, are never recovered and propagate as the teacher is updated from the student. We propose SNOAR, a self-training framework that corrects the teacher's estimates before use: the noise leaked into its speech estimate is removed by differential noise filtering (DNF), and part of the noisy observation is added back in to restore suppressed speech and attenuate artifacts. We show that the two corrections depend on each other, as without DNF the loop collapses to the identity mapping. Compared to RemixIT, SNOAR is more stable along training and outperforms it in signal-based, perceptual, and word error rate metrics, reaching 97\% of the SI-SDR improvement of a fully-supervised topline on WHAM!; on real CHiME-3 recordings, it improves every metric of three different teachers, while RemixIT degrades their perceptual quality.

classification.tldr: 提出无需干净参考语音的自训练去噪框架，通过差分噪声滤波和观测回加在训练前修正教师估计，在WHAM!上达到全监督基线的97%性能。

papers.title: SNOAR: Self-training with Noise filtering, Observation adding, and Remixing for Speech Denoising Without Clean References

papers.abstractEn: Phonetic error detection (PED) aims to identify phoneme-level substitutions, deletions, and insertions and is essential for educational and clinical speech assessment and intervention. Despite recent advances in speech models for phoneme recognition, their ability to reliably detect fine-grained phonetic errors remains unclear because of a lack of high-quality evaluation data. To address this gap, we introduce PEDBench, the first PED benchmark spanning a continuum from natural to controlled speech. It comprises real-world recordings of spoken errors made by children (N=334), scripted error productions by human actors (N=1,188), and synthetic error productions generated using phone-conditioned text-to-speech (N=1,083). All phonetic annotations were transcribed and verified by two phonetically trained annotators. Our evaluation of 13 state-of-the-art speech models shows that they fail to reliably detect phonetic errors, even under controlled conditions with acted and synthetic speech, where acoustic variability is reduced. The models also exhibit low precision, frequently misclassifying correctly pronounced phonemes as errors. Our speech-language models, fine-tuned on synthetic data, outperform commercial and open-source baselines on word-level PED, although a sim-to-real domain gap remains. We plan to publicly release our code and recipes, along with our acted and synthetic datasets, to support the development of more accurate PED systems.

classification.tldr: 发布首个语音音位错误检测基准PEDBench，涵盖真实、表演和合成错误数据，评测显示13个语音模型均难以可靠检测音位错误。

papers.title: PEDBench: Can Speech Models Detect Phonetic Errors?

papers.abstractEn: Full-duplex spoken language models decide at every frame whether to take the floor, defining a conversational personality -- yet each set of weights encodes exactly one, which human speakers bracket rather than share. Existing controls mostly act from outside; none identifies the quantity that sets how much the model speaks. We identify it: a single late-layer residual-stream direction, the initiative vector, extracted from the model's own conversations without training or annotation. The same direction reads the decision, anticipating onsets up to 800 ms ahead, and shifts it: scaled during generation, it moves speech ratio from 6-12% to 42-61% (no steering: 21-30%), consistently across conversations, weights, and corpora. A short reference recording suffices to transfer a speaker's turn-taking style to the model, and the transfer is reference-specific: swapping in another speaker's reference worsens the match in 93-98% of cases, whereas the best uniform dose is indistinguishable from no steering. Turn-taking style is not frozen into the weights but a direction that can be read, shifted, and calibrated per person. Audio examples are available at https://elpsykongloo.github.io/initiative-vector/.

classification.tldr: 该文在全双工语音模型中定位出决定发言时机的'主动权向量'，通过沿该残流方向缩放可调节模型说话比例，并仅用短参考录音即可迁移特定说话人的轮替风格。

papers.title: Reference-Guided Turn-Taking Style Transfer for Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models

papers.abstractEn: Head-related transfer function (HRTF) spatial upsampling from sparse measurements is a fundamental challenge in personalized binaural audio. We formulate HRTF upsampling as an operator learning problem and introduce SPARO, a neural operator that maps sparse measurements at a set of spatial directions to the HRTF field, a continuous representation that can be queried at arbitrary positions. SPARO projects the measurements onto a learned set of spherical latent modes, processes the latent modes with Transformer blocks, and decodes the resulting representations at query directions. On SONICOM, using the LAP24 measurement configuration, SPARO attains the best log-spectral distortion (LSD) and interaural level difference (ILD) error at every sparsity level from 3 to 100 measurements (18% lower LSD and 43% lower ILD error than the strongest baseline at 100 measurements) while remaining competitive in interaural time difference (ITD) error. It reconstructs a dense HRTF 15 to 373 times faster than the leading neural-field method RANF. We further validate the approach on HUTUBS, demonstrating its effectiveness across HRTF datasets.

classification.tldr: 将HRTF空间上采样建模为算子学习问题，提出基于球面潜模式与Transformer的神经算子，在稀疏测量下取得更低的谱失真与耳间误差并大幅加速推理。

papers.title: HRTF Upsampling and Personalization via Neural Operators

papers.abstractEn: India's 22 scheduled languages are spoken by over a billion people in conversations that mix languages, often within one turn, overlap freely, and take place over telephones, in meetings, and in media. Knowing who spoke when, the task of speaker diarization, is essential to speech applications for such conversation: voice agents conversing with several people at once, speaker attributed transcription of meetings and calls, contact center analytics, and media monitoring. We present a systematic study of speaker diarization across all 22 languages on IndicDiarBench and introduce Anuvani-Diarization, which adapts a self-supervised end-to-end segmentation model to Indian conversation with uncertainty aware silver supervision. Evaluated zero shot alongside nine recent diarization systems, it reaches a duration weighted diarization error rate (DER) of 16.78% on all 1,164 recordings, the lowest of all systems we ran and second only to the best published result (16.0%), and leads the three strongest rivals in 14 of 22 languages. It matches its parent on six international benchmarks. We also show that the benchmark's utterance level annotation convention is a hidden variable worth 1.9 to 4.1 DER points, depending on the system, and that a convention learned from other Indian transcriptions does not transfer.

classification.tldr: 论文提出面向印度22种语言的零样本说话人日志基准与自监督端到端分割模型，在低错误率上位居前列，并揭示了标注约定对评测结果的显著影响。

papers.title: Anuvani-Diarization: Zero Shot Speaker Diarization and Annotation Conventions Across 22 Languages

papers.abstractEn: Every multilingual speech pipeline begins with a language decision, an error there propagates silently through recognition, translation and routing. In India it spans 22 scheduled languages across four language families, heard over short, noisy, narrowband and code-mixed audio. Foundational speech models increasingly present language identification (LID) as an inherent latent, generalized capability. Autoregressive decoders in speech models emit a special language ID token, and modern LLMs with audio capabilities can name the language when prompted. We test this assumption on identical clips and find that whisper and similar speech models has tokens for only 15 of the 23 languages, on one second inputs Gemini 3.5 Flash reaches 0.52 macro-F1 and GPT-audio 0.14. We present Anuvani LID, a dedicated 115M parameter LID conformer model trained on 54,643 hours of Indian speech spanning 22 Indian languages and Indian accented English. Along with designed and controlled studies on 102 condition benchmark with speaker and corpus held out tests. Across 37 conditions, it reaches 0.914 mean macro-F1, 5.2 points above Gemini 3.5 Flash and ahead of 14 other systems. It is 24 points ahead of Gemini at one second, scores 0.897 on all 23 languages where no other system exceeds 0.713, and is calibrated to an ECE of 0.008. Reliable Indian LID still requires a robust, dedicated and calibrated model.

classification.tldr: 训练一个专用于印度22种语言的1.15亿参数语音语言识别模型，在37种条件下宏F1达0.914并具备良好校准，显著超越通用语音大模型的隐式语言识别能力。

papers.title: Anuvani-LID: Robust and Calibrated Spoken Language Identification for Indian Languages

papers.abstractEn: Speech-capable language models inherit most of their knowledge from text-rich language backbones, and continued model maintenance is likewise dominated by text updates. Knowledge acquired through a text update can nevertheless remain difficult to access when the same query is spoken. We formulate this mismatch as post-update speech access repair, where the knowledge-bearing checkpoint stays frozen and a detachable operator repairs speech-only access in one model pass. We introduce Affine Fields for Interface Repair across Modalities (AFFIRM), which first learns and freezes a base correction for speech hidden states, then adds query-specific corrections with zero mean over the operator-training queries. Paired speech and text states provide the coordinates that condition these corrections on each query. On balanced synthetic-speech PopQA, paired comparisons do not establish a clear advantage for AFFIRM over global SALSA steering or low-rank ReFT interventions under the same frozen single-state constraint. On recorded SLUE-SQA-5 questions with text passages, a full-scale PopQA-fitted AFFIRM operator transfers without refitting and improves ROUGE-L by 0.0941 over its paired No Repair baseline. Low-rank ReFT interventions also transfer positively, whereas the matched SALSA variant falls 0.0707 below its paired baseline. These results show that text acquisition and speech access can diverge after an update and should be verified and repaired separately.

classification.tldr: 针对文本更新后语音查询无法访问新知识的问题，提出冻结主干、以仿射场算子修复语音隐状态的方法，在真实语音问答数据上无需重新拟合即可提升ROUGE-L。

papers.title: Repairing Speech Access After Text Updates with Frozen Affine Fields

papers.abstractEn: Full-duplex speech systems must decide when to enter, hold, or relinquish the conversational floor, even as multiple speakers overlap or backchannel without taking it. Existing evaluations study dyadic turn-taking or end-to-end agent behavior, but lack a unified, controlled evaluation of genuine floor transitions against confusable non-events in multi-party settings. We introduce MultiPartyTurnBench (MPTB), a benchmark of 240 synthetically generated, channel-separated conversations spanning two to five speakers and six interaction types. MPTB evaluates two complementary tasks: End-of-Turn (EOT) detection distinguishes genuine turn completion from temporary holds, while Interruption (INT) detection distinguishes successful floor takeovers from non-floor-taking speech. Exact event-conditioned annotations enable causal evaluation using false-positive-constrained recall and signed latency. Across acoustic, semantic, and turn-projection baselines, we find a stark asymmetry: learned systems achieve 82.5-92.6% EOT recall at 4.3-11.8% false-positive rates, while INT detection suffers from missed takeovers or excessive false activations. This asymmetry extends to five full-duplex agents which achieve 86.1-95.8% balanced accuracy on turn entry, yet perform near chance (46.9-54.7%) on selective interruption handling. Gemini-3.8-Live yields to 97.7% of backchannels, whereas MiniCPM-o-4.5 yields to only 1.4% of genuine interruptions. These findings establish selective floor control as a distinct, unresolved challenge for reliable multi-party voice interaction.

classification.tldr: 发布多说话人语音对话的轮次控制基准，包含240段合成对话和事件条件化标注，评测发现模型在结束轮次检测上较强但在选择性打断处理上接近随机水平。

papers.title: MultiPartyTurnBench: Benchmarking Floor Control in Multi-Party Spoken Dialogue

papers.abstractEn: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) models and Audio LLMs fail when vocal tone contradicts textual semantics. Extensive training on congruent data engenders a rigid semantic prior, causing "Semantic Dominance", a severe text bias during cross-modal conflicts. We introduce the ASPIRE benchmark of adversarial audio-text pairs across four conflict types, alongside two metrics: Semantic Overconfidence Penalty (SOP) and Latent Decoupling Degree (LDD). Unlike fusion methods that merely re-weight collapsed features, our Acoustic Conflict Resolution Network (ACR-Net) uses Cross-Modal Attention and Contrastive Decoupling Loss to disentangle contradictory representations into orthogonal latent spaces. Experiments show existing models fail under polarity conflicts due to extreme semantic overconfidence. Conversely, ACR-Net preserves acoustic fidelity, maintaining high LDD to drive SOP near zero, achieving superior Acoustic Accuracy (ACC) in both adversarial and standard scenarios.

classification.tldr: 揭示语音情感识别中声学与文本语义冲突导致的语义主导偏差，提出对比解耦网络分离矛盾表征，并发布对抗性音频-文本基准与两项评测指标。

papers.title: ACR-Net: Mitigating Semantic Dominance via Contrastive Acoustic-Semantic Decoupling

papers.abstractEn: Reliable fault detection is crucial for industrial machinery in large-scale facilities, where unexpected failures can cause costly downtime and production interruptions. Although acoustic monitoring provides a scalable solution for machine condition monitoring, its deployment is often constrained by high false-positive rates. We propose a two-step approach to automatic anomalous sound detection: first, when only normal operating audio samples are available, a regularized unsupervised model is deployed; then, after the first machine fault, a few-shot adaptation strategy exploits the anomalous samples acquired during the fault to improve the system. This adaptation increases the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPR) from 23.0 to 64.0 and improves detection in the low false-positive-rate region, with the partial area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (pAUROC) increasing from 39.6 to 72.8. We also show that covariance regularization improves both prediction accuracy and training stability in the unsupervised model. These results provide a practical strategy for acoustic anomaly detection systems, enabling improved accuracy and reduced false alarms.

classification.tldr: 提出一种两阶段声学异常音检测方法，先以正则化无监督模型监测设备，再在首次故障后利用少量异常样本做少样本自适应，将AUPR从23.0提升到64.0并显著降低误报率。

papers.title: Few-Shot Adaptation for Anomalous Sound Detection at Low False-Positive Rate

papers.abstractEn: We introduce SEA-HELM Audio, a Southeast Asian (SEA) multilingual evaluation framework that extends the text-based SEA-HELM benchmark to assess performance degradation in cascaded automatic speech recognition and large language model (ASR-LLM) pipelines. Using synthesized speech, we compare speech-input and text-input performance across five languages (Chinese, English, Malay, Indonesian, and Tamil) on multiple-choice reasoning and instruction-following tasks. We evaluate open-weight and commercial ASR-LLM systems using identical verifiers and quantify the speech gap as the difference between text and speech accuracy. Results show substantial degradation, with accuracy drops of 9.00 to 18.50 percentage points for multiple-choice reasoning and 20.00 to 42.86 points for instruction following. Tamil exhibits the largest degradation, exceeding 40 percentage points. Our findings highlight the limitations of text-only benchmarks in predicting voice-agent reliability and demonstrate the value of SEA-HELM Audio for evaluating multilingual voice-agent systems.

classification.tldr: 构建东南亚多语言ASR-LLM级联管线评测框架，量化语音输入相对文本输入的准确率下降，发现推理和指令跟随任务均存在显著语音鸿沟。

papers.title: SEA-HELM Audio: Evaluating Multilingual ASR-LLM Pipeline Performance Across SEA-HELM Subsets

papers.abstractEn: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. We evaluate the proposed dataset across three tasks: self-supervised representation learning, vessel-type classification, and MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Experiments on DeepShip and ShipsEar demonstrate the effectiveness of ONCship for acoustic representation learning, with joint pre-training on ONCship and AudioSet achieving a classification accuracy of 62.45% on DeepShip through linear probing. Furthermore, incorporating ONCship as auxiliary training data improves downstream vessel-type classification performance. Beyond conventional vessel-type classification, we further investigate MMSI-Level Vessel Classification, treating each vessel as a distinct identity. Experimental results show that models fine-tuned with different loss functions achieve Top-1 accuracies exceeding 53% and Top-5 accuracies approaching 69%, demonstrating the feasibility of distinguishing individual vessels through MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Overall, ONCship provides a valuable resource for underwater acoustic representation learning and vessel recognition, while its rich vessel-level metadata enables further exploration of MMSI-Level Vessel Classification.

classification.tldr: 发布了一个4521小时的大规模水下声学船舶识别数据集ONCship，并在表征学习、船型分类和MMSI级个体识别任务上验证了其有效性。

papers.title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition

papers.abstractEn: Post-training often improves the performance of large audio-language models on audio understanding and reasoning benchmarks. However, these improvements may reflect adaptation to specific question formats, such as multiple-choice questions, rather than genuine advances in audio understanding and reasoning capabilities. To investigate what LALMs actually learn from post-training, we conduct controlled experiments that disentangle improvements in audio understanding from adaptation to specific question formats. Across different models and post-training methods, we find that much of the reported improvement persists even without informative audio, but largely disappears when the question format changes. These findings suggest that post-training often teaches models to exploit task-specific textual cues and answer patterns rather than developing generalizable audio understanding and reasoning capabilities.

classification.tldr: 通过受控实验剖析音频语言模型后训练收益的来源，发现其改进多源于对选择题等任务格式的适应而非真实音频理解与推理能力的提升。

papers.title: What Does LALM Post-training Learn? Rethinking Audio Understanding and Reasoning Capabilities

papers.abstractEn: Massively multilingual speech modeling has made remarkable progress in recent years, yet existing training resources and benchmarks still underrepresent much of the linguistic long tail. To address this gap, we introduce ELARSpeech, a large-scale multilingual speech resource comprising 30,202 hours of speech across 675 underrepresented languages, curated from the Endangered Languages Archive.
